comments.body: 2026-10-05: cause not pinned from code; the run log is on another machine. Three paths could hand a wake over twice: (1) codex queue succeeded but the pane still read idle/waiting 5 s later, so unanswered_commands typed it too - log msg.rang via=command, msg.ring.command_untaken, then a typed msg.rang; (2) codex queue outlasted PATIENCE (5 s; the 223 MB binary can sit >15 s in _dyld_start) and was killed after storing - msg.ring.command_failed refused=false, then a typed msg.rang; (3) the pane participant left behind when the agent named itself (fixed as a_2cW57OXLB) re-rung from outstanding() after a restart/takeover - daemon.started or a takeover between the read and the second ring. Ruled out: the declared wait re-ringing (went_idle fires only on Idle, and says still unread). Paths 1 and 2 type the second copy on purpose (a wake too many over one lost); changing that needs evidence of which fired. Check the next occurrence's daemon log against these.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: 2026-10-07: not reproduced, unchanged. The OpenAI account hit its usage limit until 2026-11-02, so no real turns could be timed. The card's paths are in the doorbell's harness-agnostic command-wake code.

comments.body:
Three more Codex instances, from GitHub issue #2 part 9 and its two comments (Muster 0.15.0):

- Undated: in a two-member group, the wake for #5 arrived twice. The first read returned the message; the second wake arrived after the reply (#6), and the read returned "nothing unread".
- 2026-10-13, macOS: a wake for #74 arrived again after the pane had read it, done the review and posted #78. `muster msg read --group <same group>` returned `nothing unread`.
- 2026-10-13, macOS: a peer-group wake for #43 was read and reviewed, the findings posted as #45, the turn ended, and the identical wake for #43 arrived and started another turn. Both the group and the team group had nothing unread.

In every instance so far, the repeat arrived after the agent had answered and ended its turn.

And one from Claude Code on 0.15.0 (tooling feedback, 2026-10-12), so the `codex queue` paths above cannot be the whole story. A harness-agnostic path to check: `doorbell.rs`'s module doc says a ring given up with its text still in the prompt is sent by the next ring that finds that text. That matches a stale wake line seen left unsubmitted in an idle worker's prompt the same day. The same day also had one notice naming two groups that had already been read.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: Claude Code instance 2026-10-17, Mac mini, a helper pane in a private project, adapter reporting. At 12:51:39 I ran muster msg read --group <its group with its maker> and it printed #7, #8 and #9. About ten minutes later Muster typed '3 new (#7-9), 1 urgent, 3 to you ... still unread' into my prompt. It was not submitted until the sender pressed Return for me (submitted 13:01:57 per my transcript), and a read then printed nothing. muster window showed me idle the whole time. A Claude Code 'Heads up' banner was showing above the prompt, which may also be why the Return was lost (see the late-urgent-ring report on the feedback board, a_2iUefqPcQ there). So: the stale-wake recheck is still missing, and a typed wake can be left unsubmitted.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: A worse variant, same round, 2026-10-20 (Muster 0.16.2-dev, Codex pane, adapter reporting, daemon connected): right after the integrator typed /new into the Codex pane and posted a new brief (#14), the wake arrived but muster msg read returned 'nothing unread'. So a new message was counted as read before the agent read it, and a worker that trusted msg read would have sat idle with its assignment unseen. Possibly tied to the /new reset.

comments.body: 2026-10-21: cause found and fixed on main (d83a509f..24151394). Every Codex duplicate on this Mac (11 on 10-20..22) followed msg.ring.command_untaken: codex queue stored the wake, a Codex without the shared app-server (daemon_auto_start = false here) polls its queue every ~10 s, the doorbell typed its fallback copy at 5 s, and Codex then delivered its stored copy as that turn ended - right after the agent's own post. The command wake now gets 20 s (COMMAND_ANSWER) before it is typed; a test with a fake session that takes its wake 8 s late failed before the fix. Measurement in docs/observations/codex-0.163.0.md. The Claude Code sightings are a different path, now a_2lxWzorui. Full gate pending (disk).

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-05, Muster 0.13.0, codex-cli 0.159.0 on the laptop (adapter reporting, so `codex queue` wakes were available), group mixed-demo: the director posted #11 `--to p297eckk7w`. The agent was woken, ran `muster msg read`, did the work, and posted #16. It then got a second, identical wake for #11; `muster msg read --group mixed-demo` answered `nothing unread`. It reported this itself as #17.

One wrinkle: #11 asked it to run `"$MUSTER_DAEMON" report --waiting "director test"`, so it declared itself waiting during that turn, and `muster window` still shows it `waiting` afterwards.

Unverified guesses: (a) the `codex queue` wake started the turn after the 5 s fallback had already typed a ring, so both arrived; (b) the waiting state made the doorbell re-ring once the turn ended. The run log for the window has both wake paths.
title: 📬 A Codex agent got a second wake for a message it had read and answered
